The world

Search Engine Land, ppc.land · 22 Sep 2026

Google auto-enrolled Shopify merchants into AI checkout, opt-out only

On 22 September, Google switched on native checkout inside AI Mode and the Gemini app for eligible Shopify merchants, without an opt-in request: products became purchasable directly inside Google's AI surfaces through the Universal Commerce Protocol, and sellers who want out have to find the agentic-commerce setting and turn it off themselves. Contentgrip reported the change also quietly shifts how Google attributes the resulting sales.

Why it matters the default has flipped from “ask before you're in” to “you're in unless you notice,” the same mechanic driving this issue's historical bridge, just wearing an AI Mode badge instead of a mail-order catalog.
Social Media Today, Shopifreaks · week of 19 to 25 Sep 2026

Meta expands the cap that turns free Facebook reach into a paid feature

Meta is broadening a limited December 2025 test: more non-paying Facebook Pages are now capped at two link posts a month, with a pop-up offering to lift the limit for subscribers to Meta One for Business. Links dropped in comments, or pointing to Meta's own apps, don't count against the cap, only links inside the post body to outside sites.

Why it matters Meta had already told advertisers that link posts get very little organic reach; now it is charging Pages for the privilege of posting the low-reach format anyway, monetizing a behavior it previously discouraged.
Campaign US, PRWeek, Netinfluencer · appointment Jun 2026, event 5 to 8 Oct 2026

Advertising Week New York opens 5 October with a YouTuber running creator programming

Netinfluencer's 28 September creator-economy calendar flags Advertising Week New York as next week's headline event: Dhar Mann, whose moral-conflict videos draw 170 million followers and roughly 300 million weekly views, was named the conference's first “chief creator officer” back in June and will open the show with a keynote plus a 100 million dollar Creator Challenge meant to generate new creator-brand deals. A dedicated Creator Day will pair working creators with CMOs for short one-on-one sessions.

Why it matters an advertising trade conference is no longer inviting a creator as a guest speaker, it hired one to run part of the agenda, which is a different level of institutional buy-in than a panel slot.
New Market Pitch, The Sauce · September 2026 recap

Creator economy funding hits 1.39 billion dollars in a single month

Twelve publicly announced creator-economy funding deals in September totaled more than 1.39 billion dollars, with Whatnot and ElevenLabs (500 million dollars at a roughly 11 billion dollar valuation, Series D led by Sequoia) accounting for about 75% of the disclosed total. Six of the twelve rounds were Series A. Five of the twelve funded companies, Levanta, Astute, Passionfroot, Nectar Social and Devotion, build infrastructure that helps brands manage creator relationships, the single most repeated category in the batch.

Why it matters the money is flowing mostly to the plumbing that connects brands to creators, not to creators directly, which is the investor's version of the same institutionalization Advertising Week just made official.

Social trends

Google Trends, Printway, Mars · hot, saturated by late Sep 2026

Halloween goes from nascent to saturated before October even starts

  • Google's search-interest score for “Halloween 2026” hit 100 in July, already above October 2025's peak of 75, driven by the “Summerween” pattern on TikTok and Pinterest; Mars previewed more than 120 seasonal candy products back in May under “Halfway to Halloween.”
  • 31 October falls on a Saturday for the first time since 2020, a weekend that has historically lifted costume and decor sales 12 to 18%, per seller-timeline data from Printway.
Why it matters already saturated. Brands that waited for October to start posting are arriving at a trend most of the category began seeding in early summer.
Newengen · nascent, Sep 2026

The cozy fall montage

  • Slow mornings, warm drinks, candles, layered outfits, studying by a window: an unbranded montage format built entirely on ambient autumn mood rather than a joke or a hook.
  • Tracked by Newengen's Instagram trend roundup dated 23 September 2026 as one of the platform's clearest current low-production, high-completion formats.
Why it matters nascent, not yet claimed by any single creator or brand.
SocialPilot, Clipchamp · hot, unquantified, Sep 2026

“The bob”

  • Multiple trend trackers are calling 2026 “the year of the bob,” with creators posting transformation and styling content arguing for the cut.
  • No platform-verified view count or audio-use figure is published for the trend as a whole; flagged as such here.
Why it matters hot per aggregate trend coverage, unquantified at the platform level.

Campaigns & brand moves

Touchpoint News, Media Key, Engage · launches 3 Oct 2026, Italy

MediaWorld turns 35 and puts 60 million euros behind nostalgia

“35 Years of WOW Moments. Together,” signed by Armando Testa with media planning by Starcom, launches 3 October with a film tracing MediaWorld's path from its first Italian store, opened in Curno in 1991, to its most recent opening, framed as a symbolic bike tour between the two. The 2026 marketing budget stays at roughly 60 million euros, with a second campaign wave, an X Factor sponsorship and a Sanremo activation already planned for 2027.

Why it matters a retailer built on discounting is spending its anniversary budget on memory instead of a sale, betting that thirty-five years of “first moments” sell more loyalty than one more price cut.
Engage, Media Key, Il Giornale d'Italia · on air 28 Sep to 25 Oct 2026, Italy

AXA Italia says every age is the right age

“L'eta non dovrebbe essere un rischio” (Age shouldn't be a risk), created by Publicis Conseil and localized for Italy by LePub Milano with media planning by Wavemaker, extends AXA's global “Know You Can” manifesto into a new chapter about demographic change: the spot shows different generations supporting each other through personal milestones. It runs on TV, connected TV, on-demand, web, social and in roughly 900 Italian cinemas through 25 October.

Why it matters an insurer is selling reassurance about aging by showing intergenerational support instead of actuarial tables, turning a demographic problem the whole industry is quietly worried about into the emotional center of the ad itself.
Marketing Dive · published 23 Sep 2026, runs through 31 Oct, US

Target hides its own product to sell “design”

“Inside Out” shows Target purchases, from a dog leash to a birthday cake, materializing as if from an invisible version of the brand's own red shopping bag, set to Raye's “Joy,” in 30- and 15-second spots across broadcast, streaming, radio, digital and social. Creator-made “Red Bag Stories” content runs alongside “Bagspotting” activations in Boston and Chicago in early October, where locals photographed holding a Target bag receive a gift card on the spot.

Why it matters Target is treating its own carrier bag, the cheapest, most disposable object in the entire transaction, as the brand's most recognizable asset, worth a national campaign of its own.

Content that works

Socialinsider 2026 Social Media Benchmarks · analysis of 69 million videos

TikTok's average engagement rate is falling while YouTube Shorts climbs

Socialinsider's 2026 data puts average engagement at 2.60% on TikTok, down from 3.70% in 2025, and 0.45% on Instagram Reels, down slightly from 0.48%. YouTube Shorts is the only platform to rise, from 0.27% to 0.30%. Within TikTok, 15-to-30-second videos earn the highest engagement rate (6.00%), while 120-to-180-second videos earn roughly 11 times more median views than short clips. Separately, Buffer's posting-frequency data shows accounts posting 2 to 5 times a week earn up to 17% more views per post than weekly posters, rising to 34% at 11-plus posts a week.

Why it matters the platform that built the short-form playbook is the one now losing engagement fastest, which is the actual, measurable reason brands are pouring money into creator infrastructure rather than more branded posts, per this issue's funding number above.

The historical bridge

NEW YORK, 1926

The book club that invented the opt-out default

Advertising copywriter Harry Scherman and three partners started the Book-of-the-Month Club with a mail-order pitch, “30 Great Books for 2.98 dollars,” and a subscription mechanic nobody had run at that scale before: each month, the club's selection arrived automatically and billed the subscriber, unless the subscriber actively said no in time and chose an alternate title instead. Record and CD clubs copied the same “negative option” model for decades. It became so widely abused, silent enrollment, buried cancellation instructions, that the Federal Trade Commission wrote its first Negative Option Rule in 1973, and in 2024 finalized a “click-to-cancel” amendment requiring cancellation to be as easy as sign-up (a court vacated that specific rule in 2025 on procedural grounds; the FTC is rewriting it).

Why it still holds. Google's Shopify auto-enrollment and Meta's expanding link-post cap are the same mechanic, dressed in software instead of a mail-order envelope: the default is now “you're in,” and the customer carries the burden of finding the opt-out. Scherman's innovation was treated as a regulatory problem within fifty years. It took the platforms of 2026 about as long to reach for the same lever.
